newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan tax rise not seen affecting M2+CDs growth.
newsitem.headline: Japan tax rise not seen affecting M2+CDs growth.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth of 3.1 percent in April did not seem to have been affected by a rise in Japan's sales tax, a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official and analysts said on Friday.
"April's growth was within our quarterly outlook of about three percent growth," the BOJ official said.
The official said an increase in Japan's sales tax did not appear to be affecting Japan's money supply growth greatly.
The BOJ said earlier on Friday that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew a preliminary 3.1 percent in April from a year earlier.
This compares with a revised 2.8 percent year-on-year growth rate in March.
The BOJ official said the growth in M2+CDs in April was due to an increase in CDs.
He said he could not comment about the implications of the money supply growth for the economy.
Japan's money supply seems to have shrugged off April's rise in the consumption tax, said Michael Hartnett, senior economist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
He said the higher-than-expected growth of M2+CDs in April is a positive sign for the the economy.
"M2+CDs is probably the best leading indicator of nominal economic activity in Japan," Hartnett said.
"Any acceleration in the growth rate of the broad money supply should be associated with an acceleration, three or four quarters later, in the nominal economy," he said.

Hartnett said that although the increase in M2+CDs is now too slow for the BOJ to consider raising interest rates, a further increase in the money supply growth rate is likely over the course of the year.
An rising trend in capital expenditure and "faint signs" of an increase in bank lending indicate that further acceleration of money supply growth is likely, Hartnett said.
"Although I do not think we will see anything pronounced in the next couple of months, the trend of money supply will be upwards rather than downwards (this year)," he said.
The BOJ said CDs increased a preliminary 21.6 percent in April year on year, compared with a revised 12.6 percent increase in March.
Friday morning's preliminary 3.1 percent growth figure was above the 2.5 to 2.8 percent range of forecasts by economists polled by Reuters.
